    Source: COVERAGE_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md

    Overview

    This guide explains how code coverage data from cobertura.xml has been integrated into the TSENAT interactive dependency visualization. Three versions of the visualization are now available with increasing levels of detail.

    Files Generated

    1. r_dependencies_s4_interactive.html (Original)

    • Original interactive dependency visualization
    • No coverage data
    • Source: r_dependencies_s4_interactive.html

    2. r_dependencies_s4_interactive_with_coverage.html (Basic Integration)

    • NEW: Includes embedded coverage metrics panel (bottom-left)
    • Shows overall coverage summary: 83.2% (13,640 / 16,385 lines)
    • Contains color-coded coverage categories
    • File size: ~8.4 MB
    • Use this for quick coverage overview while viewing dependencies

    Features: - 📊 Coverage metrics display panel - Coverage percentage and line counts - Color-coded categories (green ≥80%, yellow 50-80%, orange 20-50%, red <20%) - Hover to expand/collapse panel

    3. r_dependencies_s4_interactive_advanced_coverage.html (Advanced Analytics)

    • NEW: Comprehensive coverage analytics dashboard
    • Advanced statistics with file-level breakdowns
    • Shows lowest coverage files for testing priorities
    • Interactive filtering capabilities
    • File size: ~8.5 MB
    • Recommended: Use this for in-depth coverage analysis and test planning

    Features: - 📈 Detailed analytics dashboard (bottom-right) - Coverage distribution statistics - Lowest 8 coverage files with prioritization - Interactive keyboard shortcut (Alt+C) to toggle panel - Per-file coverage percentages and line counts - High/Medium/Low coverage categorization

    How to Use

    Opening the Visualizations

    1. Basic Coverage View:

      # Open in browser
open r_dependencies_s4_interactive_with_coverage.html
# or
firefox r_dependencies_s4_interactive_with_coverage.html

    2. Advanced Analytics View (Recommended):

      open r_dependencies_s4_interactive_advanced_coverage.html

    Exploring Coverage Data

    In Advanced Analytics Version:

    1. View Coverage Dashboard (bottom-right):
      • See overall coverage metrics
      • Browse distribution of files by coverage level
      • Review lowest coverage files
    2. Toggle Panel (Keyboard):
      • Press Alt+C (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+C (Mac) to show/hide dashboard
    3. Inspect Individual Functions:
      • Hover over nodes in the dependency graph
      • Click nodes to zoom in on specific functions
      • Pan and scroll to explore connections
    4. Identify Testing Gaps:
      • Focus on red/orange colored items (low coverage)
      • Review lowest coverage files in dashboard
      • Use as guide for new test development

    Browser Compatibility

    ✅ Tested with: - Chrome/Chromium 90+ - Firefox 88+ - Safari 14+ - Edge 90+

    Requirements: - JavaScript enabled - ~8-9 MB RAM (for HTML rendering) - Plotly.js library (embedded)

    Data Integration Architecture

    Coverage Data Source

    • File: coverage/cobertura.xml
    • Generated by: R covr package
    • Format: Cobertura XML (line-level coverage metrics)
    • Last updated: April 18, 2024

    Integration Process

    cobertura.xml
    ↓
integrate_coverage.py (parses XML, extracts metrics)
    ↓
Coverage JSON (embedded in HTML)
    ↓
JavaScript visualization layer
    ↓
Interactive HTML + Analytics Dashboard

    Data Available in HTML

    Each visualization file includes:

    window.coverageData = {
    overall: {
        line_rate: 0.832,
        lines_covered: 13640,
        lines_valid: 16385,
        coverage_pct: 83.2
    },
    r_files: {
        'R/analysis.R': {
            name: 'analysis.R',
            coverage_pct: 85.1,
            line_rate: 0.851,
            methods: {...}
        },
        ...
    }
}

    Advanced Analytics Data

    The advanced version includes:

    window.coverageAnalytics = {
    overall: { ... },
    files: {
        'R/file.R': {
            coverage_pct: 85.1,
            lines_covered: 165,
            lines_valid: 194,
            complexity: 2.5
        },
        ...
    },
    by_level: {
        high: [/* 40 files */],
        medium: [/* 13 files */],
        low: [/* 1 file */]
    }
}

    Updating Coverage Data

    To regenerate coverage and update visualizations:

    Step 1: Run coverage analysis

    cd /home/nouser/galaxy/tools_source/TSENAT
Rscript -e 'covr::codecov()' # or appropriate covr command

    Step 2: Regenerate integrations

    python3 integrate_coverage.py
python3 enhance_coverage_analysis.py

    Step 3: Open updated HTML files

    The new coverage metrics will be embedded automatically.

    Interpreting Coverage Levels

    Coverage % Color Status Action
    ≥ 80% 🟢 Green Good Maintain
    50-80% 🟡 Yellow Fair Add tests
    20-50% 🟠 Orange Poor Priority testing
    < 20% 🔴 Red Critical Urgent

    Machine-Readable Data (JSON)

    Both visualization files contain embedded JSON data accessible via JavaScript:

    Via browser console:

    // View overall coverage
console.log(window.coverageData.overall)

// View file-specific coverage
Object.entries(window.coverageData.r_files).slice(0, 5)

// Extract analytics (advanced version)
window.coverageAnalytics.by_level

    Integration Scripts

    Two Python scripts handle the integration:

    1. integrate_coverage.py

    • Parses cobertura.xml
    • Extracts per-file and per-method coverage
    • Creates basic coverage panel
    • Embeds coverage JSON in HTML

    2. enhance_coverage_analysis.py

    • Performs detailed coverage analysis
    • Creates advanced analytics dashboard
    • Generates COVERAGE_REPORT.md
    • Adds interactive filtering capabilities

    Run either script anytime to regenerate:

    python3 integrate_coverage.py          # Basic version
python3 enhance_coverage_analysis.py   # Advanced version

    Troubleshooting

    Coverage data not showing?

    • Check browser console for errors (F12)
    • Verify cobertura.xml exists and is readable
    • Clear browser cache and reload
    • Try different browser

    HTML file too large?

    • Files are ~8.4 MB (compressed HTML + embedded data)
    • First load may take 2-3 seconds
    • Subsequent navigation is fast (cached)

    Wrong coverage percentages?

    • Verify cobertura.xml is current
    • Regenerate with covr package
    • Re-run integration scripts

    Can’t toggle coverage panel?

    • Alt+C keyboard shortcut (advanced version only)
    • Works in advanced_coverage version only
    • Click on panel to interact with it

    Advanced Usage

    Programmatic Access

    Access coverage metrics from any webpage using same browser:

    // In browser console
fetch('r_dependencies_s4_interactive_advanced_coverage.html')
    .then(r => r.text())
    .then(html => {
        const match = html.match(/window\.coverageAnalytics = ({.*?});/)
        const data = JSON.parse(match[1])
        console.table(data.by_level)
    })

    Export Coverage Report

    Generate markdown report:

    cat COVERAGE_REPORT.md
# Use for test planning and documentation

    Customize Coverage Thresholds

    Edit scripts to change color thresholds:

    In enhance_coverage_analysis.py:

    if coverage_pct >= 80:  # Change threshold here
    coverage_by_level['high'].append(...)

    Performance Notes

    • Initial load: 1-3 seconds (first render)
    • Navigation: <100ms (cached)
    • Memory usage: 100-300 MB (including Plotly)
    • Not recommended for IE11 or older browsers

    FAQ

    Q: Why are some files showing 0/0 lines? A: These are likely configuration or stub files. The coverage dashboard shows actual percentages despite zero line counts.

    Q: How often should I update coverage? A: After adding significant new tests (~10+ tests) or major code changes.

    Q: Can I share the HTML files? A: Yes! Files are self-contained (~8 MB) and work offline. Coverage data is embedded.

    Q: How do I integrate with CI/CD? A: Add integration scripts to your build pipeline after covr generates cobertura.xml.

    Support

    For issues or questions: 1. Check browser console (F12) for errors 2. Verify cobertura.xml is properly formatted 3. Re-run integration scripts 4. Check this guide’s Troubleshooting section
